title: Thad Jones, bass trombone and his teachers
summary: Thad Jones got him back to tenor trombone; he had been the main Black bass trombonist, learning from Tommy Mitchell, Bart Varsalona and Tony Studd.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: Learning your horn: teachers, lessons and fees

blocks.x: And Thad Jones got me to go back to the tenor trombone. I was playing bass trombone all the time, you know, during all the recording sessions and all that because there was no good colored bass trombone players around yet.

Jack Jeffers was just coming on the scene and Benny Powell was still with Basie. He hadn't come off the road with Basie yet, you know. And I was the only one, actually, playing bass trombone. And I had a ball with it. And I practically learned that myself, too, but Tommy Mitchell taught me a lot, Bart Varso (ng), I would ask him a million questions when I saw him about the horn, and Tony Studd was my greatest teacher.
Oh, he's great. I'd tell him today --
